conviction_note: Nothing decisive found: a competitor's (Stryker/Inari) supply backorder through ANGO's whole Jun-Aug quarter and an easy NanoKnife comp with Medicare LCD live from 5 July lean positive, against the toughest mechanical-thrombectomy comp of the year (Q1 FY26 MT +41%) and a single-source Q1 consensus ($80.9m, +6.9%) that sits above the company's own FY27 guided growth of 5-6.5%; findings sum +0.5, scaled number 0.25 (p_up 51 x abs 12.5), and the name has sold two clean beats in 2026 (-13.5% each), so the reaction function keeps p_up at a coin flip.

findings.finding: Stryker said on its Q2-2026 call (2026-07-31) that a supply disruption at one Inari plant created a significant backorder and lost peripheral-vascular sales (US vascular organic -6.7%), with backorders expected back to a manageable level only by the END of calendar Q3 - i.e. the market leader's VTE clot-removal line (FlowTriever/ClotTriever) was supply-constrained across ANGO's entire fiscal Q1 (June-August 2026), a window in which AngioVac/AlphaVac (MT, $11.1m in FQ4, ~14% of sales) could pick up cases; consensus and the EW preview frame MT as a stalled franchise after FQ4's -1.1%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: MT was the growth story through FY26 (+41% in Q1 FY26, +17.9% in Q3); the Q3 FY26 print with MT +17.9% still fell -13.7% (Apr 2026), and FQ4 with MT -1.1% rose +1.7% on the guide, so this line has not visibly driven the reaction on its own.
findings.why_not_priced: The Inari backorder is in a large-cap's call and is not in any ANGO preview read (EW 2026-09-30 discusses only ANGO's own sales-force reset and competition as headwinds). If priced, the preview narrative would be MT share recapture and the stock would not have slid 6.9% into the print. Caveat sized in: Penumbra (US revenue +17.1% in Apr-Jun) is the more obvious beneficiary, and the disruption already overlapped part of ANGO's FQ4 (Mar-May) in which MT still declined, so the share pickup may be small; net of the rest of the company MT is only ~14% of sales.
findings.independence: Proxy (counterparty statement, not confirmed by ANGO). Search-summary corroboration of the same call: https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/stryker-q2-earnings-call-highlights (same document, counts once). Penumbra Q2-2026 8-K shows US revenue +17.1% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001321732/000132173226000036/pen-63026xexhibit991.htm) - VTE demand healthy, but Penumbra may be taking the share.

findings.finding: Mechanical thrombectomy faces its toughest comp of the year in FQ1: Q1 FY26 MT was $11.3m, +41.2% (8-K 2025-10-02), while the run-rate had fallen to $11.1m and -1.1% in FQ4 with AngioVac -15.8%, prompting a commercial reorganization ('changed our commercial approach... new leadership structure'); flat sequential MT would print roughly -2% YoY, a second straight decline, against a VTE market where Penumbra grew US revenue 17%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FQ4 (Jul-2026) MT -1.1% was masked by a total beat and above-consensus FY27 guide; stock +1.7%. No print yet where MT decline was the headline.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the EW preview (2026-09-30) names the MT stall as the key question. What is not in the preview is the arithmetic that the YoY comp is the hardest of the year, so a 'second MT decline' headline is likely even if sales stabilise sequentially. If fully priced, the preview would not need to frame the sales-force reset as an open question. Netted for the rest of the company: MT is ~14% of sales; Auryon (+mid-teens guide) and NanoKnife (easy comp) need only hold trend to carry Med Tech to the +12-15% guide.
findings.independence: FQ4 MT numbers and reorganization: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001275187/000114036126028368/ef20077916_ex99-1.htm and call highlights https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-7-14-angiodynamics-inc-stock/ (company documents, different dates). EW preview flags the same concern: https://earningswhispers.com/article/ANGO/20302.

findings.finding: NanoKnife enters FQ1 with an easy comp ($6.4m in Q1 FY26 vs $11.8m, +64.5%, in FQ4) and its Medicare coverage framework went live inside the quarter: Palmetto GBA's final LCD L40205 for IRE in favorable intermediate-risk prostate cancer became effective 2026-07-05, on top of Category I CPT codes effective 2026-01-01; management called probes (FY +28.7%) the bellwether and warned FQ4 capital (+132.5%) was lumpy.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NanoKnife +64.5% in FQ4 coincided with only +1.7%; the stock has not paid much for this line on its own.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the LCD was press-released in May and EW calls NanoKnife 'the counterweight'. What remains is magnitude: the first full quarter of covered Medicare prostate cases against a $6.4m comp could produce +40-60% growth, which is a meaningful contributor to Med Tech's +12-15% guide. If fully priced the stock would not trade 7% lower into the print. Lands inside the company's Med Tech guide, so sized small.
findings.independence: Hospital program launches continue (UnityPoint St. Luke's, June 2026: https://www.unitypoint.org/news-and-articles/press-releases/unitypoint-health-st-lukes-first-in-metro-to-offer-new-minimally-invasive-prostate-cancer-treatment). Year-ago NanoKnife $6.4m from the Q1 FY26 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1275187/000114036125037060/ef20056554_ex99-1.htm), shared with the MT-comp finding.

findings.finding: Earnings Whispers (2026-09-30) reports FY27 consensus revenue of $325.1m, below the low end of the company's $336-341m guide, and Zacks moved ANGO from Strong Sell to Hold on 2026-10-05 (an estimate-revision-driven rank); if the street really sits under the guide, a simple reaffirmation at FQ1 forces estimates up.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The July 2026 initial guide ($336-341m vs $314m consensus) bought +1.7%; the Oct-2025 FY26 guide raise with a beat bought +6.1%.
findings.why_not_priced: Disputed bar: the $325.1m figure is single-source and may be stale (Finviz quoted $314m pre-guide); Q1 consensus of $80.9m is consistent with the guide, which suggests most analysts already model it. If the gap were real and priced, the stock would trade on reaffirmation odds; capped small because the bar cannot be confirmed.
findings.independence: Zacks rank change Strong Sell -> Hold 2026-10-05 (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/ANGO/price-target/); pre-guide consensus $314m (https://finviz.com/news/367694/angiodynamics-tops-revenue-forecasts-and-raises-sales-outlook-for-fiscal-2027-ango).

findings.finding: The CEO succession has a hard date that the print sits inside: the FY26 10-K (filed 2026-07-14) says Jim Clemmer retires on the earlier of 2026-11-30 or the appointment of a successor, the board said it expected a successor in the first half of FY27 (Jun-Nov 2026), and no successor has been announced as of 2026-10-07; the FQ1 release/call is the natural venue to name one or to address the timeline.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The retirement announcement rode with the Jan-2026 FQ2 beat and the stock fell -13.5% (Motley Fool attributes the drop to the CEO uncertainty: https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/01/06/why-angiodynamics-stock-is-sinking-today).
findings.why_not_priced: The deadline is in the 10-K risk text, not in the preview. A named successor would remove the overhang that cost 13.5% in January; no name with seven weeks left would extend it. Sign is genuinely two-sided, hence the wide band and a small positive centre (naming is more likely than not with the deadline seven weeks out, but who is named matters).
findings.independence: Jan-2026 8-K announcing the search and first-half-FY27 expectation: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1275187/000114036126000341/ef20062354_ex99-1.htm. Searched for an appointment release and found none.

findings.finding: Q1 consensus revenue of $80.9m (+6.9% YoY) sits above the company's guided full-year growth of ~5-6.5% even though Q1 carries the hardest MT comp and management said Q1 'is usually a step down' from Q4; a segment build from company numbers (Auryon $16.5m x1.14 = $18.8m, MT ~$11m, NanoKnife ~$8.5-9m, other ~$1.1m, Med Device ~$40.4m at the guided 'flat') gives ~$80m, about 1% under the bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats were sold in Jan and Apr 2026 (-13.5%, -13.7%); revenue has beaten consensus at every print since Q1 FY26 ($75.7m vs $72.7m, Oct 2025, +6.1%; $86.6m vs $80.2m, Jul 2026, +1.7%), so the company habitually clears the bar.
findings.why_not_priced: It is my inference from company numbers, not a reported fact; the consensus itself is single-source. If the market saw a miss risk the whisper would sit below consensus, but the EW whisper on EPS is better (-$0.06 vs -$0.10). Sized small: the company has beaten the revenue bar four prints running, and Med Device (52% of sales) could easily run +1-2% instead of flat.
